newsitem.title: USA: American Home sees 1997, 1998 net rising.
newsitem.headline: American Home sees 1997, 1998 net rising.

text.p: American Home Products Corp Vice-President of Investor Realtions Thomas Cavanagh said on Thursday he expects the company's earnings and sales to improve in 1997 and 1998.
Cavanagh declined to give a specific range of the company's expecetd financial results. American Home Products reports its second quarter results on Tuesday July 22.
Cavanagh said he expects the company to increase its dividend this year, which would mark the company's 46th year of consecutive dividend increases.
American Home Products reported 1996 sales of $14.1 billion and net income of $1.9 billion, or $2.96 per share.

American Home Products expects the approval of six new major products during 1997, including Duract, a pain reliever that was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) two days ago. American Home Products also expects approval for treatments of hemophilia and depression, as well as Alesse, an oral contraceptive for women.
Cavanagh said the company's product pipeline now includes more than 60 new products.
Cavanagh expects the company to submit for FDA approval six major products in 1998 and in 1999.
One of the major products expected for filing in 1998 is a vaccine to treat middle-ear infections in children.
